transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me today. 

Um... I want to make sure I give you the right information, so I'll just try to be completely honest, even though it's... well, it's a little shameful to admit. I really don't want to sound dramatic or make a big deal out of nothing, but I came in because I just keep having these thoughts that it would be better if I didn't wake up in the morning. 

And... I hope it's okay to say this, I don't want you to think badly of me, but sometimes I feel like dying would just be the fair punishment for what I've done to my family and to my flooring crew. Does that... does that make sense why I'd feel that way? I'm sorry to start off with something so heavy right away.

Before this current period of low mood, have you ever gone through a stretch of days or weeks where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or irritable, needed much less sleep, or felt like your thoughts were racing?

No, no, I don't think so. I mean, I'm usually just... trying to keep up with everything. I've never really felt super energetic or, you know, on top of the world like that. And I definitely need my sleep to do my job, hauling around all that carpet and tile. 

I try really hard to be easy to work with, so I don't think I've ever been unusually irritable or anything... at least, I hope I haven't been. I'd hate to be a burden on my crew. Does that answer what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.

Have you ever experienced a period like this before—weeks or more of feeling deeply down, losing interest in things, and having low energy—at some other time in your life, separated by a stretch where you felt back to your normal self?

Um, well... I'm not entirely sure if I've had a time where it went away completely and came back. I just know that this... this heavy feeling, it's been with me for a while now. 

I really don't want to complain, because I know people go through much worse, but I think it's been about a year and two months now. It started a few months after my husband got injured. I've just felt so down since then. I try to put on a brave face for him and the crew, but it's just been a constant struggle since that happened. 

I hope it's okay that I can't remember if there was a time before this... I just know this current stretch has been going on for over a year. Is that the kind of timeline you were looking for? I'm sorry if I'm not explaining it very well.

You mentioned feeling like dying would be a fair punishment for what you've done to your family and crew—can you tell me more about that? Do you feel you've actually done something terribly wrong, or have you had any experiences like hearing voices or seeing things that others don't seem to notice?

Um... well... I really hope this doesn't make me sound crazy or awful. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there, nothing like that, I promise. But... 

I just... I keep thinking that I'm the reason my husband got worse after his injury. And because I was so distracted and terrible at my job, the crew lost work, and I just feel like I messed up our clients' homes. It sounds so silly when I say it out loud to a doctor, but I just have this overwhelming feeling that I've poisoned everything I've touched lately. And that's why I feel like I deserve whatever bad things happen to me. 

I know it's probably just me overthinking things, right? I'm so sorry, I don't mean to sound like I'm throwing a pity party or anything. Does that make sense, though? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question the right way.

When you think about being the cause of your husband's condition or the crew's lost work, do you feel completely certain that this is true and real, even if someone showed you evidence it wasn't your fault—or is it more that you feel this way emotionally, while knowing deep down it might not be entirely accurate?

Um... well, it's... it's hard to explain without sounding like I'm completely losing my mind, and I really, really don't want you to think I'm crazy. But... I guess it's not just an emotional feeling. 

Even on the days when I'm not, you know, crying or stuck in bed... I just... I get this absolute certainty about things. Like, with the jobs... I know the homeowners and the suppliers are watching me. I can tell they're using the floor patterns we lay down, and the texts they send, and even the calls for the building permits... they're using all of that to track me. To prove that I'm ruining the jobs on purpose. 

My husband and the crew, they try to tell me I'm just stressed, that nobody is doing that, but... I just know it's true. No matter what they say, they can't talk me out of it. It feels so real to me. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds so strange and probably not what you wanted to hear. I just... I'm trying to be as honest as I can so you can help me. Is it okay that I feel that way? I really hope I'm not making things too difficult for you to understand.
